Apply knowledge to understand AI interaction.

slides.title: AI APIs: The Waiter Analogy
content: Connecting your applications to AI
slides.narration:
Welcome to this tutorial.
We will explore AI APIs today.
This is a key concept.

slides.narration:

slides.title: System Requirements
content: Computer with internet access
Web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, etc.)
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you will need:
A computer with internet access.
And a web browser.
For example, Chrome or Firefox.

slides.title: Prerequisites
content: Basic understanding of Artificial Intelligence.
Familiarity with web applications.
slides.narration:
Before starting, ensure you have:
A basic understanding of Artificial Intelligence.
And familiarity with web applications.
slides.image_prompt: A slide with text 'Prerequisites' and icons representing a brain (for AI) and a web browser or app screen (for web applications).

slides.title: Introduction to AI APIs
content: The most important concept for understanding how AI is used.
slides.narration:
Let's start with AI APIs.
This is a crucial concept.
It helps us understand how AI is used.
It connects your apps to powerful AI models.
slides.image_prompt: A diagram showing a user application connecting to a cloud service labeled "AI Model" via a layer labeled "API". Arrows show data flow between them.

slides.title: Analogy: Restaurant Waiter
content: An API is like a Restaurant Waiter
slides.narration:
Imagine you're at a restaurant.
You want a hamburger.
You are like your application.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person sitting at a restaurant table, looking at a menu. A thought bubble above their head shows a hamburger.

slides.title: The Kitchen (AI Model)
content: You don't go into the kitchen to cook it yourself.
slides.narration:
You don't cook it yourself.
The kitchen is the complex AI model.
It does the heavy lifting.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a bustling restaurant kitchen with chefs cooking, representing the complex inner workings of an AI model.

slides.title: The Waiter (The API)
content: You give your order (a prompt) to a waiter (the API).
slides.narration:
Instead, you give your order.
This is your prompt.
You give it to a waiter.
The waiter is the API.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a waiter taking an order from a customer at a restaurant table. The customer is holding a smartphone labeled 'Application' and the waiter has 'API' on their uniform.

slides.title: The Order Process
content: The waiter takes your order to the kitchen, which prepares your food.
slides.narration:
The waiter takes your order.
They go to the kitchen.
The kitchen prepares your food.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a waiter walking from a customer's table towards a kitchen door, holding a notepad with the order.

slides.title: The Delivery (AI Response)
content: The waiter then brings the finished dish (the AI's response) back to your table.
slides.narration:
Then the waiter brings it back.
The finished dish is the AI's response.
It comes back to your table.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a waiter serving a finished dish (e.g., a hamburger) to the customer, who looks pleased. The dish has a label 'AI Response'.

slides.title: What is an API?
content: An API (Application Programming Interface) is that waiter.
slides.narration:
So, what is an API?
It is the Application Programming Interface.
It acts as that waiter.
It's a messenger.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing "Application" -> "API (Messenger)" -> "AI Model" with arrows indicating flow. The API icon is highlighted.

slides.title: API as a Messenger
content: It takes a request from your application, sends it to the AI model, and returns the model's response.
slides.narration:
It takes your request.
It sends it to the AI model.
Then it returns the model's response.
Think about it.
It connects your app to powerful AI.
slides.image_prompt: Animated graphic: an arrow from 'App' to 'API', then 'API' to 'AI Model', then 'AI Model' to 'API', then 'API' to 'App'. Each step is clearly shown.

slides.title: API Keys & Requests
content: Understanding how to interact with AI services.
slides.narration:
Now let's discuss API Keys.
And also API Requests.
These are important for interaction.
slides.image_prompt: Section header: 'API Keys & Requests' with icons for a digital key and a message bubble or an envelope, symbolizing communication.

slides.title: API Key Explained
content: This is a secret password. It’s like your unique ID card.
slides.narration:
An API Key is a secret password.
It's like your unique ID card.
It proves your permission.
To the restaurant, like Google or OpenAI.
You can place an order.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a digital key icon with 'API Key' text, next to a padlock or a secure ID card.

slides.title: Keeping API Keys Private
content: You must always keep your API key private!
slides.narration:
You must keep your API key private.
Always protect it.
Sharing it can be risky.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a locked safe or a shielded key icon, with a prominent 'Do Not Share' sign, emphasizing privacy and security.

slides.title: What is a Request?
content: This is the act of placing your order.
slides.narration:
A Request is placing your order.
In code, you send your API key.
And also your prompt.
To the AI service.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person holding a smartphone or computer, sending a message labeled 'Request' which includes a key icon and a text prompt.

slides.title: Summary
content: An API is a messenger for AI.
Analogy: Waiter in a restaurant.
API Key: Your secret ID.
Request: Sending your prompt and key.
slides.narration:
In summary, we learned:
An API is an AI messenger.
It's like a waiter.
An API Key is your secret ID.
A Request sends your prompt and key.
These connect your apps to AI.
slides.image_prompt: A slide with a bulleted list summarizing the key concepts, perhaps with small illustrative icons next to each point.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Think of an app you use.
How might it use an API to connect to an AI?
Write down your idea.
slides.narration:
Now for an assignment.
Think of an app you use daily.
How might it use an API?
To connect to an AI service?
Write down your idea.
Share it with a friend.
slides.image_prompt: A slide with text 'Assignment' and an illustration of a person thinking, with thought bubbles showing various app icons and a connection to a cloud AI.
